queries: IFBench instruction following benchmark frontier models fail generalize constraints

sources_considered.why: MultiChallenge paper (Scale AI), revised March 2025. Reports that all frontier models scored under 50% on a multi-turn test that needs accurate instruction following.
IFBench paper (Ai2), July 2025. Tests GPT-4.1 and Claude 3.7 Sonnet, both available at the post date. Published after the target period, so used as context only.
Current MultiChallenge leaderboard. Shows scores for spring-2025 models, but the measurement dates are unclear (updated 2026). Context only.

receipt.public_excerpt: all frontier models have less than 50% accuracy on MultiChallenge, with the top-performing Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024) achieving just a 41.4% average accuracy.

evidence_items.explanation: In early 2025, every frontier model tested failed more than half of realistic multi-turn tasks. The paper says these tasks need accurate instruction following. That fits 'still seems lacking'.

receipt.public_excerpt: All 4 challenges require accurate instruction-following, context allocation, and in-context reasoning at the same time.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows that the benchmark tests instruction following, though not on its own; it also tests context use and reasoning.

receipt.public_excerpt: we introduce IFBench with new, diverse, and challenging verifiable instruction following constraints where leading models such as GPT-4.1 or Claude 3.7 Sonnet score below 50%.

evidence_items.explanation: Models released before the post scored under 50% on unseen but verifiable instructions. Published after the target period, so it is context only.

receipt.public_excerpt: Figure 1 shows that models display good accuracy on IFEval.

evidence_items.explanation: Partial counterpoint: on the simpler and widely used IFEval benchmark, models already scored well. The same paper says this reflects overfitting, not general reliability.

unresolved_gaps: I could not read OpenAI's GPT-4.1 launch page (HTTP 403), which reports its own MultiChallenge and IFEval scores.
No single agreed measure of 'reliable' instruction following exists. Results vary by benchmark.
